h: The Third Meal Leads From Torah to Divine Cleaving

p: At the Friday night meal we say,
"to see the radiance of Ze'ir Anpin,"
וְאִיתָא בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ, חֵלֶק ג נד, ב)
And it says in the holy Zohar (this parshah, III 54b):
וְכֵן כָּתַב רַבִּי חַיִּים וִיטַאל זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה
and so wrote Rabbi Chaim Vital, of blessed memory.
that is, the river that goes out of Eden, etc.
And it says: "What is 'they would scorn him'?
this is the Holy One, blessed be He;
and not to be bound with her:
when it says, "they cannot extinguish," etc.?
if the Holy One, blessed be He, gives
how could they scorn one who merited
from the Holy One, blessed be He?
that even one who has merited
Chochmah and Binah and words of Torah,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם יָכוֹל הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע לִשְׁלוֹט
the yetzer hara can nevertheless rule;
on the contrary, "whoever is greater than his fellow,
And even one who has merited
מִכָּל מָקוֹם יָכוֹל הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע לִכְנוֹס
the yetzer hara can nevertheless enter,
with the four who entered the Pardes (Chagigah 14b);
the ones who have no share in the World to Come
and merited precious and pleasant wealth,
and nevertheless they were pushed out
of the community of Yisrael in the Mishnah.
And this is what it said: "'If a man would give':
this is the Holy One, blessed be He;
and not to be bound with her":
as long as there is no union
and unification of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah,
And this is what it said, "If a man would give":
for the Holy One, blessed be He, is called,
as it were, by the name "man,"
as we said in explaining the holy Zohar
there is no revelation of the Kingdom of Heaven,
"Your throne is established from of old" (Tehillim 93:2).
"For they have no desire at all
that Knesses Yisrael is bound to Him,
to the Holy One, blessed be He,
Now on Shabbos, the whole day
is the unification of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah;
that for this reason the Minchah prayer
begins "You are One and Your Name is One,"
for then is the complete unification
and it corresponds to the Shabbos of the future,
Hashem will be One and His Name One"
And this is what is written in the holy Zohar:
in joy, in light, in blessings," etc.
given to a person on Erev Shabbos
is alluded to in the verse
and why is it not alluded to on Erev Shabbos?
is chiefly at the third meal.
"For no man can see Me and live":
but in their death they see;
that is, death by a kiss,
when they merit the revelation of the Shechinah
and the soul cleaves to its root
like a candle in a torch.
of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah,
we merit "to see the radiance of Ze'ir Anpin."
And at the third meal there passed away
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב קנו, א)
as written in the holy Zohar (II 156a);
and the three of them are the root of words of Torah:
is the root of the Written Torah;
and David HaMelech, peace be upon him,
a chariot for the attribute of Malchus,
פֶּה תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה קָרֵינַן לָהּ
"the mouth, we call it Torah she'b'al peh";
and Yosef is the drawing forth
they would have been given only
the five books of the Torah
and the book of Yehoshua alone,
for it is the arrangement of Eretz Yisrael."
וְהַיְינוּ חֵלֶק שֶׁל כָּל אֶחָד מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל
That is, the portion of each one of Yisrael
which is from the attribute of Malchus,
And the three of them are the root of the holiness of Shabbos:
to make a Shabbos meal for the Shevatim,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה, מִקֵּץ צב, ד)
as they said (in Bereishis Rabbah, Miketz 92:4):
"Moshe rejoices in the gift of his portion," etc.;
and he fed the whole Generation of the Wilderness with the manna,
and had he entered Eretz Yisrael,
it would have remained so forever,
that Yisrael would be free for Torah alone:
"And strangers will stand and tend your flocks,
and you will be called priests of Hashem,
as it will be in the future.
And David is a chariot for the attribute of Malchus,
Therefore the three of them passed away on Shabbos,
for then they merited the unification
of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah,
like a candle in a torch.
nor set up a beis midrash then,
and corresponding to them we say
And the reason is not mourning,
for then they would mark the remembrance
and not on days of the week.
Rather, since that is the time of unification,
there is no place then for words of Torah,
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ חֵלֶק ב פב, ב)
(as written in the holy Zohar II 82b);
for how to merit the utterance "I am";
Torah learning was implanted in their hearts
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה, יִשָּׁקֵנִי, א, ב)
(as they said in Shir HaShirim Rabbah on "Yishakeini," 1:2);
and at the time of unification,
when we merit to be bound with her,
there is then no leisure for words of Torah;
to see the radiance of Ze'ir Anpin,
which is the cedars of Levanon,
while the Written Torah and the Oral Torah
And through Chochmah and Binah alone
for a person's inclination overpowers him,
and "whoever is greater than his fellow," etc.;
and it could be, Heaven forbid,
as with those who entered the Pardes.
מַיִם רַבִּים לֹא יוּכְלוּ לְכַבּוֹת וְגוֹ׳
at the Friday night meal and in the morning
we say the song before the meal,
and at the third meal after the meal.
And so our holy masters were accustomed
at the Friday night meal and in the morning
which is not so at the third meal,
when they do not say words of Torah;
do they say the song and the words of Torah.
that at all the Shabbos meals
it is not the main unification,
and we say words of Torah
which is not so at the third meal,
for at the time of the prayer and the meal
and then is the time of the unification
of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah;
we do not say words of Torah then,
there is no leisure for words of Torah;
for the whole point of words of Torah
for how to attain the utterance "I am"
of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah.
And after the unification we say,
"to see the radiance of Ze'ir Anpin,"
we merit to see the radiance of Ze'ir Anpin.
And afterward we say words of Torah
to draw the holiness from Shabbos
that come toward us in peace,
that they hold on to the holiness of Shabbos,
